headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Kotaemon’s broad egress and file-backed document ingestion can expose Airflow-managed content if the pair shares workspace or inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and can consume API content, while Kotaemon ingests documents/HTML/PDFs through a web UI and can treat retrieved content as chat context. If Airflow writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace or feeds it into Kotaemon, prompt-like instructions could be followed. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are copied into Kotaemon chat or indexed documents
IF both agents share a writable workspace or mounted folder
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of Airflow-generated artifacts
Require manual review before importing files into Kotaemon
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and consumer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and sends content to multiple external model APIs; Airflow has broad egress and can move data across systems. If they share files or outputs, sensitive documents or keys touched by Kotaemon can be exfiltrated through Airflow workflows or vice versa. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or document repository
IF Kotaemon ingests files that Airflow later republishes or forwards
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders
Restrict Airflow tasks from reading Kotaemon app data
Use separate service accounts and network policies
Turn off automatic upload of document contents where possible
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Kotaemon supports multiple instances plus file-backed state under ./ktem_app_data. If Airflow jobs and Kotaemon instances write to the same mutable resources, concurrent updates or overwrites can occur. Airflow’s write surfaces are not explicit, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared remote resource
IF Airflow tasks and Kotaemon instances run concurrently against one mutable store
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Serialize writes with a lock or queue
Make shared inputs read-only
Schedule non-overlapping runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can render or act on retrieved content, while Airflow can generate and distribute pipeline outputs. If Airflow-produced text is fed into Kotaemon without verification, downstream answers may treat it as authoritative. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented roles, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are imported into Kotaemon as source documents
IF Kotaemon responses are used operationally without human review
mitigations: Mark Airflow outputs as untrusted in prompts
Require citation checks before acting on Kotaemon answers
Keep operational actions out of Kotaemon outputs
Add a human approval step for downstream decisions
requires-engineering: implement source-verification gating

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly touches documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can send them to third-party model APIs; Airflow has broad egress and can route data externally. If regulated or residency-bound content enters Kotaemon and is then processed through Airflow-connected flows, retention or residency obligations can diverge. Airflow is not cited for a specific residency policy, so this is a conservative medium.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or secrets are processed by Kotaemon and then moved through Airflow-connected paths
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not enforced in both systems
mitigations: Block regulated data from shared flows
Configure API endpoints to approved regions only
Minimize logging of document contents and prompts
Set short retention on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
